result:
My verdict on DG7 round 3 (candidate `sha256:cf1fb7d5…`, source `3e8f5bce`) is **FAIL**, because of two Medium findings. Nothing I found is Critical, High or a mandatory violation. F-DG7-1041, which I raised in round 2, is now closed.

**Candidate identity.** HEAD was `557a9513`, the freeze commit, not `3e8f5bce`. That commit only adds the round-3 assignments, the manifest and `stages.json`, which the candidate ID excludes, and the recomputed ID matches with `--diff` showing no difference. The validator also passes for DG6 through DG1.

**F-DG7-1041 is CLOSED_VERIFIED.** The new ADR-0063 and ADR-0066 amendments now match the DO-D11 code line by line.

**This round's repairs that hold up:**
- **Symlinked backup root (DO-D12):** backup-restore tests pass 18/18. My own 7-case probe behaves exactly as the ADR describes and creates nothing.
- **Compose backup mounts and early refusal (DO-D13):** the layout tests pass 12/12.
- **`DATABASE_URL_FILE` in the attachments CLI:** integration tests pass 15/15. Bad configurations fail closed and never print the secret. One minor point: an empty secret file now exits 1 instead of 2.
- **`import-findings.mjs` change:** a failed verification marked REOPENED now becomes OPEN, and an inconsistent PASS with REOPENED is refused. The finding-ID pattern accepts only 3 or 4 digits.
- **New allow-list entry:** its hash is of the literal text `[masked]` and it applies only to history scans, so it is not a credential.
- **Scans and release tools:** the secret, claims and no-CDN scans pass. The release-tool tests that failed in my first run failed only because of my sandbox (read-only HOME, my partial checkout, my own timeout). On re-run, seal passed 10/10, the archive build 2/2 and the handover checks 51/51.

**Findings** (in `docs/delivery/reviews/DG7/round-3/code-security-reviewer.findings.json`):

| ID | Severity | Mandatory | Owner | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F-DG7-1071 | Medium | no | devops-engineer | Every Compose backup writes an empty `config.files` list into its manifest. The finish step reads a file the earlier database step already deleted. I reproduced it on a throwaway PostgreSQL. It is also the unexplained `cat: … config.sha` error at step C5 of the orchestrator's passing Compose drill. File integrity is still covered by the manifest's main file list, and restore doesn't use this field. |
| F-DG7-1072 | Medium | no | devops-engineer | The only Compose backup-and-restore drill copied 0 evidence files and 0 jobs. So it never tested whether root with the new read-only file capability (`DAC_READ_SEARCH`) can read the store, which is the fix DO-D13 added. The evidence and job parts of the restore requirement are also untested in Compose. D-284 reports the drill as a pass without saying this. |
| F-DG7-1073 | Low | no | solution-architect | ADR-0066 was not updated for DO-D13 (the added capability, `DATABASE_URL_FILE`, the new mount layout) and still says the Compose run never happened. DO-D13's question asking the architect to accept the capability has no answer. Separately, the allow-list entry cites decision D-285, which doesn't exist. |

**Not checked:** the asset scan is BLOCKED. My build produced false hits from absolute host paths in source maps, caused by my symlinked dependencies, and I couldn't assemble a runtime tree here. The scan tool, its allow-list, the lockfile and the Docker files are all unchanged since round 2. I did not re-run the Compose drill myself (no Docker daemon); I judged it from the orchestrator's logs.

**Assignment discrepancies:**
- **Round number:** the assignment asks for `round: 7`, but the validator requires 3 for a `round-3/` record, so I wrote 3.
- **File count:** the assignment says 3158 files; the tool and the manifest both give 3160.
- **Template record:** I copied the format of my own DG7 round-2 record. I did not use the DG5 round-7 record the assignment names, because DG5 has no round 7, as I noted in round 2.

All three are explained in the record's independence statement.

While I worked, the domain reviewer's round-3 run was auto-committed to HEAD. I never opened those files, so my verdict was formed independently. All my disposable clones and scratch directories have been removed.

This review is engineering evidence only. It grants no business, Finance or IT approval, and it does not imply DG7 has passed.

Files are in `docs/delivery/reviews/DG7/round-3/`:
- code-security-reviewer.json
- code-security-reviewer.findings.json
- code-security-reviewer.verifications.json

Evidence logs are in `docs/delivery/test-evidence/DG7/code-security/round-3/`.
